text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- The head of State Property Committee Maxim Boiko says he is to raise the issue of personal security of state officials dealing with state property in the wake of the apparent contract killing yesterday of the deputy mayor of St Petersburg.
- President Boris Yeltsin at his meeting with the separatist Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov has promised the rebel republic 'some kind' of independence.
- Two Russian television crews arrive in Moscow after a long captivity in Chechnya amid rumours that a ransom was paid for their liberation.
- A new Russian Public Television crew has been arrested in Minsk.
- The government seems to be running behind schedule trying to finish work on the 1998 budget before August 25.
- The Tax Service has been debating the fate of a new group of enterprises with a major backlog of tax arrears, trying to find a way to make them pay.
- Russian cosmonauts who returned to earth last week say they are not to blame for a series of accidents which crippled the Mir space station.
- Natural gas monopoly Gazprom is to acquire controlling stakes in two major Russian newspapers.
- Shareholders in the Nizhegorodskiye Avialinii carrier have voted down a possible merger with Aeroflot.
- Viktor Paliy, head of Nizhnevartovskneftegas oil producer, at odds with company's major shareholder Alfa-group, is trying to organise a thorough audit of the group.
- The military hardware producer MAPO is awaiting reorganisation which could also include a public flotation of the company.
SEVODNYA
- President Boris Yeltsin cannot grant independence to Chechnya without violating Russia's constitution.

- The hostage crisis involving Russian television crews held in captivity in Chechnya may have been just a cynical trick played by the Chechen leadership on the eve of their meeting with President Yeltsin in Moscow.
- The murder of Deputy Governor of St Petersburg Mikhail Manevich could be a warning to people working on privatisation programmes on the national level.
- The Tax Service has drawn up a list of six big enterprises with overdue budget payments it intends to squeeze money from.
- The Fuel and Energy Ministry is undergoing profound changes brought about by the new reform-minded minister Boris Nemtsov.
- The government is putting the final touch to the draft agreement with Ukraine on sugar deliveries to Russia.
- The State Property Committee has set the date for the sell-off of its controlling stake in the Tyumen Oil Company.
- Italian steel producers have accused Russian exporters of dumping practices.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA

- Russian-Chechen negotiations in Moscow have shown that Grozny is setting the pace in relations with Moscow, that the Russian leadership does not know what to do with Chechnya and that Chechnya is moving ever-so-close to a de-facto and de-jure separation from Russia.
- The 'Tambov' criminal grouping may be behind the killing of Deputy Governor of St Petersburg.
- Russian metals smelters could see themselves running way below capacity if the government bans them from importing raw materials and exporting the finished product.
- Half Russian gold-mining companies are working at a loss.
IZVESTIA
- Moscow has proposed giving separatist Chechnya wide autonomous rights similar to those obtained by Tatarstan.
- Six years after the attempted August 1991 coup which brought down the Soviet Union, post-Soviet romanticism has given way to a pragmatism born of harsh experience.

- Russian cosmonauts aboard the Mir space station are limbering up for the hard task of repairing the crippled craft while on earth experts are working out who is to blame for a series of glitches which brought the Russian space mission to the verge of collapse.
- Organisers of the MAKS-97 airshow near Moscow are hoping new technologies will open Russia's way to world markets.
- Russia is in for an upsurge in road accidents, says the head of the Traffic Police in an interview.
ROSSISKIYE VESTI
- Russian President Boris Yeltsin after a meeting with separatist Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov in Moscow said he hoped Russia and Chechnya would stay together.

- The memoirs of former President Yeltsin's bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov are, in fact, not as interesting to normal people as they are to journalists who seem to thrive on the smell of dirty linen, says the official paper.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Moscow, like before, continues to send huge sums of money to Chechnya and then be surprised at the news it has disapeared into thin air.
- Russia is slowly turning from 'semi-bandit capitalism' towards a game played with rules, says First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov in an interview.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
